advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace `literal.lstrip("./")` with a proper `./`-prefix strip (e.g. `removeprefix("./")`) so paths with leading dots/slashes resolve correctly.
evidence: `str.lstrip` treats its argument as a set of characters to remove, not a prefix, so `'..//a.sh'.lstrip('./')` -> `'a.sh'`
advisory.finding: `literal.lstrip("./")` strips a CHARACTER SET (`.` and `/`) rather than a `./` prefix, so any script literal beginning with those characters is mangled: `"../shared/x.sh"` becomes `"shared/x.sh"` and `".hidden.sh"` becomes `"hidden.sh"`, resolving to the wrong (or non-existent) path and silently skipping the deletion scan.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `literal.removeprefix("./")` (or resolve the literal relative to the referencing test file's directory) instead of `lstrip`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve script literals against the referencing test file's directory (and/or search the repo for the basename) so a subdir-hosted script is not silently skipped, or emit a diagnostic when a `.sh` literal cannot be located.
evidence: The incident script was referenced by a computed path, but the gate only matches literals resolving relative to repo root; a real repo reference `REPO_ROOT / "infra" / "scripts" / "reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh"` yields literal `"reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh"` which `root / literal` will not find
ABSENCE: no diagnostic/log distinguishes 'literal matched no file on disk' from 'file scanned and clean'
advisory.finding: The gate resolves a script literal only as `root / literal`; a `.sh` referenced by bare basename that actually lives in a subdirectory (e.g. `str(SCRIPTS_DIR / "purge.sh")` where the AST literal is just `"purge.sh"`), or referenced via a computed path variable, fails `script.is_file()` and is silently `continue`d — the destructive-exec scan never runs, and 'checked clean' is indistinguishable from 'script never located'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Attempt resolution relative to the test file's parent directory as well as repo root, and consider warning when a `.sh` literal resolves to no file so misses are visible.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the clean-tree test to also assert that the gate actually located and scanned at least one exec'd script (positive liveness), so a zero-scan misconfiguration cannot masquerade as clean.
evidence: ABSENCE: the test never asserts that ANY script was actually located/scanned, so a resolution bug that finds zero scripts still passes this test
advisory.finding: `test_repository_tree_is_currently_clean` asserts `chk.main(["--root", REPO_ROOT]) == 0`, but given the root-only resolution the pass carries no information: it returns 0 both when the tree is genuinely clean and when no `.sh` literal in the tree resolves to a file at all. The check cannot distinguish 'scanned and clean' from 'nothing was scanned'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the seam exemption to the specific `rm` match (e.g. check whether the matched command itself is routed through the seam) rather than the entire line.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:102-107: the `_SEAM_RE.search(line)` guard is inside the per-match loop but tests the entire `line`, not the current `match`
`_RM_RE` can match multiple `rm` occurrences per line via `finditer`, so a seam on one clears all
advisory.finding: `if _SEAM_RE.search(line): continue` clears every destructive deletion on the whole line when a seam token appears anywhere on it. A line containing both a seamed rm and a bare unguarded `rm -rf "${dir}"/*` (e.g. two commands joined) is entirely exempted, masking the unguarded deletion.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `chk.find_violations` returns [] for a script whose deletion uses only `rm -r "${dir}"/*` (and one for `rm -f`), pinning the force-and-recursive conjunction in `_is_destructive`.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:53-56 `_is_destructive` returns `bool(letters & {"r", "R"}) and "f" in letters` — added behavior requiring BOTH flags

test_every_destructive_flag_spelling_is_caught only parametrizes destructive spellings (rf/fr/r-space-f/f-space-r/Rf); no case asserts that `rm -r "${dir}"/*` or `rm -f "${dir}"/*` produces zero findings
ABSENCE: search of the test file finds no fixture exercising the False branch of `_is_destructive`
advisory.finding: No negative test for `_is_destructive`: a non-destructive flag cluster such as `rm -r "${dir}"/*` (recursive only) or `rm -f "${dir}"/*` (force only) must NOT be flagged, but every passing fixture avoids the rm entirely via a guard, seam, or no interpolation. A regression dropping the force-and-recursive conjunction would over-flag with the suite still green.
scenarios: A refactor or bug that made `_is_destructive` return True for recursive-only or force-only rm — the entire suite still passes, and non-destructive test-exec'd scripts get spuriously gated.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized negative case: fixtures `rm -r "${dir}"/*` and `rm -f "${dir}"/*` must yield `chk.find_violations(repo) == []`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert that a finding's `detail` names the script literal and the correct script-side line number of the destructive deletion.
evidence: scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py:159-160 detail = `f"execs {literal} which deletes unguarded target {target!r} at {literal}:{script_line}"`
test_finding_reports_the_test_path_and_line asserts only `f.path == "tests/test_thing.py"` and `f.line == 3`, not the detail string
ABSENCE: search of the test file for `.detail` returns no matches
advisory.finding: The `Finding.detail` message reports the offending SCRIPT-side line via `at {literal}:{script_line}`, but no test asserts that detail content — the script-line pointer (the operator's actual pointer to the dangerous line) could regress silently.
scenarios: The detail string's script-line reference is dropped or points at the wrong line — operators lose the pointer to the dangerous line, and no test notices.
